children: DOHA, Qatar--Oil prices declined Monday as traders weighed expectations of a global supply surplus against renewed attacks on shipping in the Middle East and concerns over disruptions to regional oil infrastructure.
Brent crude futures for January delivery fell 1.8% to $90.87 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures for January delivery declined 1.7% to $82.01 a barrel.
Both benchmarks fell for a third consecutive week last week, with Brent losing around 3.4% and WTI declining 5.2%, as expectations of a sizable supply surplus next year continued to weigh on prices.

Oil prices have sold off sharply this month as the market focuses on the strong recovery in Middle Eastern exports in October and the associated buildup of crude oil held on tankers, according to Giovanni Staunovo, a commodities analyst at UBS. However, Staunovo said prices underestimate the combined risks of depleted inventories, recovering Chinese demand and persistent geopolitical supply disruptions.
The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations reported several incidents involving tankers in the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, including attacks on vessels near the coast of Oman.
Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's coalition forces intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Houthi militants toward the kingdom's southern region Sunday, according to the Saudi Press Agency.

Despite the continuing attacks, oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have been recovering. Transits through the waterway remained 42% below prewar levels in the seven days through Nov. 21, according to preliminary data from ship-tracking firm Kpler.

The International Energy Agency expects a global oil supply surplus of 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to 3.8 million barrels a day next year, as recovering production outpaces demand growth.

Traders are also looking ahead to a meeting of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies on Nov. 29, when the producer group is expected to discuss its output policy for 2027.
